Q: Optimisation peptide molecule structure in RdKit environment A: 
### check RDKit Version
from rdkit import rdBase
print('Version : ', rdBase.rdkitVersion)
print('boostVersion : ', rdBase.boostVersion)

# import modules
import sys
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
from rdkit.Chem import rdDepictor
from rdkit.Chem import Draw

## create peptide (pep) from aa sequence and add hydrogens
aa_seq = "GDYSHASPLRYPEGGG"
pep = Chem.MolFromSequence(aa_seq)
pep = Chem.AddHs(pep)

## create drug from SMILES and add hydrogens
drug_smiles = "CCCC1SC[C@]2(C)NC(=O)N[C@]12C"
drug = Chem.MolFromSmiles(drug_smiles)
drug = Chem.AddHs(drug)


# embed drug molecule , create 3D structure
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, randomSeed= 1234, useRandomCoords=False)
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, useRandomCoords=True) #works
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug) #, randomSeed=123)         #works
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(drug)                  ### what difference makes ??


# embed pep molecule , create 3D structure
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, randomSeed= 1234, useRandomCoords=True)   
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, useRandomCoords=True)    #works
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, randomSeed=123)        #doesnt works ValueError: Bad Conformer Id in AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(pep) 
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(pep)                 ### what difference makes ??
    
# get number of conformer created for pep (EmbedMolecule --> 1 , EmbedMultipleConfs -> more)
pep_conf=pep.GetNumConformers()
print('\n\npep conformer : ' , pep_conf)
print('pep.GetNumConformers()  : ', pep.GetNumConformers())
print('pep.GetConformer().Is3D()) : ', pep.GetConformer().Is3D())

# rdDepictor.Compute2DCoords(drug)
# rdDepictor.Compute2DCoords(pep)

## draw pep and drug to png files
Draw.MolToFile(pep, "pep_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))
Draw.MolToFile(drug, "drug_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))
    

#prints SMILES for drug and pep
pepsmi = Chem.MolToSmiles(pep)
drugsmi = Chem.MolToSmiles(drug)
print('\n\npep smiles :', pepsmi)
print('\n\ndrug smiles :', drugsmi)

#remove hydrogens from pep and drug
pep = Chem.RemoveHs(pep)
drug = Chem.RemoveHs(drug)

#combine mol and pep in same object
bonded = Chem.CombineMols(pep, drug)
# make created onject pep+drug editabel through RWMol (create mol class to be edited)
edbonded = Chem.RWMol(bonded)

# Add bond between pep atom 0 and drug atom 0 (now index +pep.GetNumAtoms()) as per OP request
edbonded.AddBond(0, 0+pep.GetNumAtoms(), order=Chem.rdchem.BondType.SINGLE)
conjugate = edbonded


# compute 2D coords of conjugate (bonded pep + drug)
# otherwise goe RuntimeError: Pre-condition Violation trying adding hydrogens ; why ?????
## AllChem.EmbedMolecule(conjugate, randomSeed=1234,  useRandomCoords=True fails to without compute2dcoords
conjugate_conf=conjugate.GetNumConformers()
print('\n\nconjugate conformer : ' , conjugate_conf)
print('conjugate.GetNumConformers()  : ', conjugate.GetNumConformers())
print('conjugate.GetConformer().Is3D()) : ', conjugate.GetConformer().Is3D())
#####################################################################
# without this I cannot go further .... ---> conjugate = Chem.AddHs(conjugate, explicitOnly=False , addCoords=True)
#                                            RuntimeError: Pre-condition Violation
#                                            getNumImplicitHs() called without preceding call to calcImplicitValence()
rdDepictor.Compute2DCoords(conjugate)
# conjugate_conf=conjugate.GetNumConformers() # not needed
###################################################################

# adds hydrogens to conjugate
conjugate = Chem.AddHs(conjugate, explicitOnly=False , addCoords=True)

#write conjugate SMILE
conjugatesmi= Chem.MolToSmiles(conjugate)
print('\n\nconjugate smiles :', conjugatesmi)


############# without this is the pdb I get is flat 2D #######
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(conjugate, randomSeed=1234,  useRandomCoords=True)

# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(conjugate,  useRandomCoords=True)
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(conjugate)       ### what difference makes ??
# conjugate_conf=conjugate.GetNumConformers()
#############################################################

print('\n\nconjugate.GetConformer() : ',conjugate.GetConformer())
print('\n[x.GetId() for x in conjugate.GetConformers()] ', [x.GetId() for x in conjugate.GetConformers()])
print('\nconjugate.GetNumConformers() : ',conjugate.GetNumConformers())
print('conjugate.GetConformer().Is3D()) : ', conjugate.GetConformer().Is3D())

# rdDepictor.Compute2DCoords(conjugate)

#draw coniugate png file
Draw.MolToFile(conjugate, "conjugate_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))


#save conjugate pdb file
Chem.MolToPDBFile(conjugate, sys.path[0]+"conjugate.pdb")

DISCLAIMER

This is just one conformer of the peptide, don't know how RDKit picks it. Could use some other tool to model it. Or have a look at EmbedMultipleConfs vs EmbedMolecule

Not sure if answer is what you where looking for because I don't know the default value of randomseed keyword in EmbedMolecule func, anyway in my attempts I get always different results *** see ADDENDUM below

ADDENDUM

https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#chem-vs-allchem

I searched more and found out that:

rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule is equivalent to rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule; Chem vs AllChem

and the function is nicely explained at rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule where randomseed defaults to -1 and as in argument explanation.

randomSeed provides a seed for the random number generator

so that the same coordinates can be obtained for a molecule on multiple runs. If -1, the RNG will not be seeded.

but there is more here:

EmbedMolecule() is no longer random?

So I get different conformers because each time I re-run my script default randomseed = -1 the RNG (random number generator) will not be seeded.

If I change :

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, useRandomCoords=True) #works
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, useRandomCoords=True)    #works

to

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug,randomSeed=1234,  useRandomCoords=True) #works
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep,,randomSeed=1234, useRandomCoords=True)    #works

I will end up with the same conformer/result.

Now I'll have to investigate useRandomCoords=True and check why using useRandomCoords=False fails, but only for the peptid (pep) or conjugate and not the drug.

Q: Converting row names to columns A:

Yes, you can do it without specifying every column by dynamically building out a "manual" unpivot.

I'm not sure of your full table schema, but adapting something like the below should work. It would be simpler if you weren't on 2016 because you could STRING_AGG... alas...

DECLARE @table sysname = N'dbo.Report';
DECLARE @sql   nvarchar(max);

;WITH c AS (
    SELECT c.name
    FROM sys.columns c
    WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID(@table)
      AND c.name <> N'ReportName'
)
SELECT @sql =
    STUFF((
        SELECT
            CHAR(10) + N'UNION ALL' + CHAR(10) +
            N'SELECT r.ReportName, ''' + REPLACE(c.name,'''','''''') + N''' AS ColumnName
              FROM ' + QUOTENAME(OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(OBJECT_ID(@table))) + N'.' + QUOTENAME(OBJECT_NAME(OBJECT_ID(@table))) + N' r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.' + QUOTENAME(c.name) + N' IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1'
        FROM c
        FOR XML PATH(''), TYPE
    ).value('.','nvarchar(max)'), 1, LEN(CHAR(10) + N'UNION ALL' + CHAR(10)), N'');

SET @sql = N'
SELECT ReportName, ColumnName
FROM (
' + @sql + N'
) x
ORDER BY ReportName, ColumnName;';


EXEC sys.sp_executesql @sql;

If you print the @sql you'll see it just results in a giant set of UNIONs wrapped up for ordering

SELECT ReportName, ColumnName
FROM (
SELECT r.ReportName, 'Acct_Num' AS ColumnName
              FROM [dbo].[Report] r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.[Acct_Num] IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ReportName, 'Address 1' AS ColumnName
              FROM [dbo].[Report] r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.[Address 1] IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ReportName, 'Address 2' AS ColumnName
              FROM [dbo].[Report] r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.[Address 2] IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ReportName, 'FirstName' AS ColumnName
              FROM [dbo].[Report] r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.[FirstName] IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT r.ReportName, 'ID' AS ColumnName
              FROM [dbo].[Report] r
              GROUP BY r.ReportName
              HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN r.[ID] IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1

... and on and on

You can see my example in action at this SQL Fiddle example

Q: Pull docker image for different architecture A:

For Rancher Desktop, when I used docker pull --platform linux/amd64, it failed:

$ docker image rmi eclipse-temurin:11-jre
Untagged: eclipse-temurin:11-jre
Deleted: sha256:19ea1e9ea1c741b73df906c4d8a6ffce8477e08074c000ea2233deb4cad3a136
$ docker pull --platform=linux/amd64 eclipse-temurin:11-jre
11-jre: Pulling from library/eclipse-temurin
Digest: sha256:19ea1e9ea1c741b73df906c4d8a6ffce8477e08074c000ea2233deb4cad3a136
Status: Downloaded newer image for eclipse-temurin:11-jre
docker.io/library/eclipse-temurin:11-jre
$ docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}' | while read image; do     printf "%-50s " "$image";     docker image inspect "$image" --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}' 2>/dev/null || echo "Error"; done
eclipse-temurin:11-jre                             linux/arm64

Instead, I had to use docker buildx --pull --platform linux/amd64:

IMAGE=eclipse-temurin:11-jre; docker rmi "$IMAGE" && printf "FROM $IMAGE\n" | docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$IMAGE" --load -

Then Rancher Desktop pulled the image with the correct architecture:

$ docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}' | while read image; do     printf "%-50s " "$image";     docker image inspect "$image" --format '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}' 2>/dev/null || echo "Error"; done
eclipse-temurin:11-jre                             linux/amd64
